chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, whom should I be kind to?' He said, 'Your mother.' He asked, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your mother.' He asked, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your father.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the most deserving of kindness according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through the chain of Muhammad ibn Abi Umair, establishes the preeminent status of the mother in filial piety, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence where her rights are often considered triple that of the father due to her unique roles in gestation, birth, and nursing. The repetition of 'your mother' underscores the cumulative weight of her sacrifices, a principle that informs the Shia legal hierarchy of parental obedience and care. This narrative complements the Quranic emphasis on gratitude towards parents, linking the spiritual merit of honoring one's mother directly to divine pleasure.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 22.Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (as) who said:

“A man came to the Prophet (sw) and asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, whom should I be kind to?’ He said, ‘Your mother.’ He asked, ‘Then who?’ He (sw) said, ‘Your mother.’ He asked, ‘Then who?’ He said, ‘Your father.’”[1]
